artworks.title: Landscape with the Fall of Icarus
artworks.description: A ploughman keeps his furrow and a galleon sails on while two white legs vanish into the green sea — the fall reduced to a splash nobody notices. Long attributed to Bruegel and now generally thought an early copy of his lost original, the painting in the Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium inspired famous poems by Auden and William Carlos Williams.

artworks.title: The Lament for Icarus
artworks.description: An oil painting by Herbert James Draper, awarded the gold medal at the 1900 Paris Exposition and now in Tate Britain. Fallen Icarus lies among mourning nymphs, his great wings still spread — the Victorian myth retold as a soft, elegiac nude rather than Bruegel's unnoticed splash, the boy become a romantic martyr of ambition.

artworks.title: The Fall of Icarus
artworks.artist: Jacob Peter Gowy (after Peter Paul Rubens)
artworks.description: An oil in the Museo del Prado painted by Jacob Peter Gowy after Rubens's design for the Torre de la Parada. Daedalus still climbs while Icarus plunges headlong, wax and feathers scattering — the Baroque fall staged as pure kinetic catastrophe against an open sky, the father's craft undone in a single dive.

artworks.title: Landscape with the Fall of Icarus
artworks.description: A panoramic mountain landscape by the Flemish master Joos de Momper, now in Stockholm's Nationalmuseum. As in Bruegel's famous treatment, Icarus is nearly lost in the vista — a tiny falling figure amid travellers and peaks — so that the myth becomes a lesson in how the world keeps moving while one boy falls.

films.title: Icarus
films.description: Vogele's Luxembourgish feature retells the Cretan myth from the boy's side — friendship with the Minotaur, distrust of Daedalus, and the choice between darkness and the sun.

films.title: Atlantis
films.description: The BBC fantasy casts Joseph Timms as Icarus beside Robert Lindsay's Daedalus — the winged son as a recurring player in a soap-opera Crete.

music.title: Flight of Icarus
music.description: Maiden's single from Piece of Mind, cut while the wax myth was pure heavy-metal material: the boy's climb becomes a son's defiance of a betraying father, and the fall a blaze of glory rather than a warning heeded.

popCulture.title: Kid Icarus
popCulture.creator: Nintendo
popCulture.description: Pit, a winged boy archer, escapes an underworld prison to save a Greek-flavoured skyworld from Medusa. The name and the wings are Icarus' own — borrowed for a flight that, for once, ends happily.

popCulture.title: Musée des Beaux Arts
popCulture.creator: W. H. Auden
popCulture.description: Auden's poem, written after standing before Bruegel's Fall of Icarus in Brussels, reads the unnoticed splash as the shape of all suffering — the ploughman keeps his furrow, the ship sails calmly on, and disaster happens off to the side.

popCulture.title: Landscape with the Fall of Icarus
popCulture.creator: William Carlos Williams
popCulture.description: Williams' short poem stares at the same Bruegel splash Auden read — Icarus a detail at the edge of a page where spring and ploughing go on.
